requirement: The first argument and first encoded field of every C_PDU is the C_PDU Type
The Type is a 4-bit field in bits 7 to 4 of octet 0 (bit 7 is the MSB)
The rest of each C_PDU's format and content is as given in B.7.1.1 to B.7.1.11
Unless stated otherwise, a field inside one octet has its lowest-numbered bit as its least significant bit (CCITT V.42 8.1.2.3)
Unless stated otherwise, a field spanning octets has bit significance falling as octet number rises, with the lowest-numbered bit as the least significant bit (CCITT V.42 8.1.2.3)
Unless stated otherwise, NOT USED bit-fields are encoded as 0
DATA C_PDU layout: octet 0 bits 7 to 4 Type = 0, bits 3 to 0 not used; the S_PDU follows from octet 1
The DATA C_PDU carries an encapsulated S_PDU from the local node to a remote node
The DATA C_PDU Type goes in the first 4-bit field and its value is 0
After the first octet, the DATA C_PDU holds the S_PDU and nothing else
A DATA C_PDU is sent with the lower sublayer's normal (not expedited) data delivery service
notes: Ed1 allowed expedited; Ed4 deprecates EXPEDITED DATA (main Table 1)

requirement: The DATA C_PDU gets the same delivery mode (ARQ or non-ARQ etc.) that SIS gave the S_PDU it carries

CAS sends a PHYSICAL LINK REQUEST to ask for a physical link to be made

requirement: The PHYSICAL LINK REQUEST Type value is 1, in a 4-bit field

The Ed4 bit is set in a PHYSICAL LINK REQUEST when the peer is known to support Ed4 or later
The Ed4 bit is not set when the peer is known not to support Ed4
When the peer's edition is unknown, the Ed4 bit may be set to discover whether it supports Ed4
